# `montage`

the standard 10-05 electrode montage on a template's scalp, with its names and its 10-20 / 10-10 / 10-05 system partition.

Version 1, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run montage --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run montage --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run montage --dataset <template package or dataset> --subject <template> [--scalp head --landmarks head_landmarks --name eeg_1005]
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `scalp` | manifold surface, where {"name": "$scalp"} | yes |
| `landmarks` | manifold points, where {"name": "$landmarks"} | yes |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scalp` | `--scalp` | `head` | - |  | the template's scalp (a closed head surface) by name |
| `landmarks` | `--landmarks` | `head_landmarks` | - |  | the points manifold of the nasion, LPA and RPA (named NAS, LPA, RPA, in the scalp's coordinate system) by name |
| `name` | `--name` | `eeg_1005` | - |  | the montage's stored name; its names are <name>_names and its systems <name>_system |
| `inion` | `--inion` | none | scalp unit |  | the inion [x, y, z] in the scalp's unit; null: nxr::meeg::inionFromLandmarks (the farthest crossing of the line from the nasion through the preauricular midpoint with the scalp) |
| `tolerance` | `--tolerance` | `1e-7` | fraction |  | Cz stops when it moves less than this fraction of the nasion - inion distance |
| `max_iterations` | `--max-iterations` | `100` | iterations |  | the most Cz iterations before refusing |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | [`geometry.surface_parts`](../nodes.md) | surface=scalp |  | vertices, faces |
| before | [`meeg.inion_from_landmarks`](../nodes.md) | vertices=vertices, faces=faces, landmarks=landmarks | inion=$inion | landmarks_with_inion |
| before | [`meeg.eeg_montage_1005`](../nodes.md) | scalp_vertices=vertices, scalp_faces=faces, landmarks=landmarks_with_inion | tolerance=$tolerance, max_iterations=$max_iterations | positions |
| before | [`meeg.montage_labels`](../nodes.md) | positions=positions |  | names, system |

`before` steps run once, `chunks` steps run on every chunk of the recording, `after` steps run once on what the chunks accumulated.

## Outputs

| output | stored as |
|---|---|
| `positions` | kind manifold, type points, name $name, derived_from scalp.manifold.0 |
| `names` | kind selection, type partition, name $name_names, on positions |
| `system` | kind selection, type partition, name $name_system, on positions |

## Notes from the definition

```text
THE STANDARD 10-05 ELECTRODE MONTAGE ON A TEMPLATE'S OWN SCALP: a recording without digitised positions can only be placed on a head by the standard system's names. The systems are RULES (positions at
fixed fractions of arcs between the nasion, the inion and the preauricular points), so the positions are computed on the head model's scalp, never read from a table (Oostenveld and Praamstra 2001, the 10-05
rule; the 10-10 names follow Jurcak, Tsuzuki and Dan 2007).

THE GRAPH:  scalp (surface) --[surface_parts]--> vertices, faces;  vertices, faces, landmarks (the points NAS, LPA, RPA) --[inion_from_landmarks]--> four landmarks;
            vertices, faces, four landmarks --[eeg_montage_1005]--> positions [345 x 3];  positions --[montage_labels]--> names, system.
Stored: the points manifold `<name>` (positions in the scalp's coordinate system, its aliases T3 = T7, T4 = T8, T5 = P7, T6 = P8 in its producer), its names `<name>_names` (one level per point) and the partition
`<name>_system` (levels 10-20, 10-10, 10-05: the narrowest system a point belongs to; the 10-10 system is the levels 10-20 and 10-10 together, the 10-05 all). `import recording --montage <name>` reads it.

What it cannot resolve: these are the SYSTEM's positions on this head model, not where a cap sits on a person; the inion is a stated convention (nxr::meeg::inionFromLandmarks, or the caller's `--inion`), not the bump the inion is.

  nxr-neuro run montage --dataset <template package or dataset> --subject <template> [--scalp head --landmarks head_landmarks --name eeg_1005]
```
